headline: Elevated, steady: Iran's claim of three tankers hitting mines in Hormuz is still not independently confirmed, and fuel prices may rise when oil markets reopen Monday.
summary: No major change since this morning. Iran's report of three tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz is still only Iran's claim, and the strait carries about 4 ships a day against 100+ before the war, so fuel remains the main risk for SA. Overnight GPS-jamming and US-flight flags were not linked to any attack: the US disruption is fallout from Friday's ground stop, blamed on a contractor's cabling upgrade, and the Microsoft 365 outage is resolved. Locally it is quiet: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no fire bans or CFS warnings, and the grid and phone networks are normal.
actions: Top up the car (and any generator fuel) before Monday, when oil markets reopen and any price rise starts flowing to SA bowsers.
Check your bushfire plan and CFS app watch zones now that the Fire Danger Season has started.

categories.summary: Iran says three tankers hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz; the claim is widely reported but damage is not independently confirmed, and the US blockade of Iran continues. Gulf GPS jamming has eased to about 11% of aircraft. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no warning signs, and forecast markets are flat or slightly lower.

categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal, no private jets are heading to retreat destinations and forecast markets show no jump. Iran's talk of leaving the nuclear treaty is a long-run concern only.

categories.summary: No Australian phone or internet carrier shows any drop and the SA grid is normal. Microsoft says its global 365 outage is resolved and was not a cyber attack, and the US flight halt was blamed on a contractor's copper-to-fibre upgrade. The global threat level is green; a Japan-led probe found about 1,000 servers used for AI-driven attacks worldwide.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: WHO reports MERS cases in Qatar and the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, with no cases outside Africa. An unverified local report of an unknown illness in western Kabul has no official confirmation. All seven Adelaide emergency departments are normal.

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges today and tomorrow, no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings. A strong wind warning is out for Spencer Gulf. Six small fires and burn-offs across SA; outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.
